title: UI Stability
summary: YTIntel now has one current app shell and one update owner, eliminating the stale v0.10.5 title and the old release-popup flicker on launch.
discord_changes: Removed the startup loop that cycled through old YTIntel update screens.
Locked the browser title, status and What’s New experience to the current v0.13.1 shell.
Refreshed the PWA cache so stale installed-app shells are retired automatically.
changes: Replaced layered shell ownership with a single stable v0.13.1 workspace controller.
Removed v0.13.0 shell execution from the current page so two workspace observers cannot fight over version state.
Marked every historical v0.10.x, v0.11.x, v0.12.x and v0.13.0 release popup as historical before legacy feature modules initialise.
Added a browser-title lock so the legacy v0.10.5 Sol module can no longer leave the tab title on an old release.
Added current-status ownership so delayed feature patches cannot downgrade the visible YTIntel version.
Added modal ownership that suppresses automatic historical popups before paint and only opens the current update when the user deliberately presses What’s New.
Added capture-level What’s New ownership so older modules can keep their feature logic even if they clone or rebind the button.
Separated chrome observers from page-navigation observers to prevent UI self-trigger loops.
Updated the service worker to network-refresh core JS/CSS assets and delete stale YTIntel shell caches after activation.
Kept Opportunity Radar, Deep Analyse, Decision Gate, Replication Check, Pattern Mine, Packaging Lab and the v0.13 workspace design intact.
why_it_matters: The app was loading the new workspace but older incremental modules were still allowed to mutate global UI state afterward. Centralising shell ownership removes that architectural conflict rather than hiding the symptoms.
